candidate_decisions.reason: The active gratitude of the servant in 17:3 and passive acknowledgment of the focus effort form a distinct, trace-supported reciprocal reading; preserve the unresolved service cue as attributed.
The supplied return, renewed-round, and habitual-return traces contact the focus course and its split return/repetition branch; retain the cross-root context roles with their limits explicit.
The native guidance, uprightness, work, and fittingness cues give the focus striving a directional and qualitative measure; unresolved context branches remain attributed.

The harm/good and haste cues in 17:11 and the immediate-seeker contrast in 17:18 jointly test desire against the later horizon and fitting work; the slow-pace branch is retained only as contextual pressure.
The attached account, readable record, and self-reckoning cues materially change whether the focus effort is treated as a vanished result or a durable, inspectable course.
The immediate-seeker contrast and 17:20's shared, unbarred provision prevent visible worldly supply from serving as a proxy for the focus's distinct acknowledgment.
The inspection, rank, magnitude, and degrees in 17:21 provide a concrete differentiated later field for the focus end and purposeful course; the stage interpretation remains qualified.
The focus believer and purposeful movement contact 17:22's rival dependence, sitting, and abandonment; retain the attributed support-failure image without treating it as literal morphology.
The registered small-input and fresh-shoot branches, joined to the supplied blessing and connected increase cues, support the complete growth analogy as exploratory rather than predictive.

The attached judgment, literal neck, and nontransferable burden support the complete emancipation analogy through the focus's labor and acknowledgment branches; the reading remains exploratory and nonliteral.

findings.title: Two Desired Horizons and Their Work
findings.claim: The immediate horizon solicits acceleration, while the later horizon joins willing to purposeful movement, work, trust, and acknowledged yield; present provision and later ranking remain beyond the worker's control.
findings.mechanism: The immediate-seeker and hastening forms in 17:18 meet the focus's later end and repeated effort. Guidance and fitting work in 17:9 give movement a route; 17:20-21 then distinguish shared present provision from later degrees.
findings.reader_payoff: The later horizon reads as a worked-for orientation rather than merely a deferred prize, and speed or abundance alone cannot certify its value.
findings.containment: The freedom-price labor branch is an analogy for movement out of immediacy, not a literal manumission sense. The trust branch is not a replacement for assent, and 17:20-21 do not promise a particular allocation. The searching branch is excluded because its own boundary rules out the focus form.

epistemic.reason: The horizon contrast and focus forms are direct; the connection to downstream allocation and the freedom-price image is contextual and bounded.

findings.title: Desire Under a Temporal Test

findings.reader_payoff: A strong or apparently beneficial wish is not self-authenticating; timing and enacted course matter.
findings.containment: 17:18-19 may contrast destinations without diagnosing every desire, and 17:11 may describe general haste. The slow-pace branch is contextual pressure only: the focus Form IV remains willing, not a direct slow-motion verb.

epistemic.reason: The contextual roots and word indices match supplied Arabic, while the account of desire's testing remains an attributed synthesis.

findings.title: Appreciation Is Not Worldly Supply
findings.claim: Present provision reaches both orientations, so visible abundance cannot by itself certify that a particular effort is appreciated; the focus acknowledgment marks a distinct relation.
findings.mechanism: The immediate-seeker clause identifies one group, while 17:20 extends the Lord's provision to both and denies that it is barred. Against that shared supply, the focus passive recognition attaches to striving rather than receipt.
findings.reader_payoff: Material provision and recognition are no longer mistaken for the same evidence.
findings.containment: The two groups' gifts may differ in kind, and 17:20 does not fully define the focus's acknowledgment. This reading rejects provision as a simple acceptance test, not every relation between gift and recognition.

epistemic.reason: The shared-provision contrast is explicit in the supplied context; its bearing on the focus valuation is an attributed synthesis.

branch_activations.carrier: The negated-barrier cue at 17:20:12, as described by the trace.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Provision is not a simple sign that one effort alone is recognized.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent gloss or facet is supplied for the unresolved cue.

branch_activations.boundary: The contextual grouping does not exhaust the focus's desire clause.

findings.title: A Differentiated Later Field
findings.claim: The focus's later end opens onto a differentiated field of degrees, so acknowledged striving need not imply one undivided outcome.
findings.mechanism: 17:21 invites inspection, sets differential rank and greater magnitude, and names degrees in the later field. Those cues return through the focus's afterlife term and purposeful movement.
findings.reader_payoff: The later horizon can contain gradation while retaining a common orientation toward it.
findings.containment: The degrees may rank final stations rather than stages or measures of striving. The verse does not state that effort alone determines rank.

epistemic.reason: The verse's inspection and degrees are explicit; applying their geometry to the focus course is an attributed macro reading.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The later horizon is presented as a field that can be examined in degrees.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent registry gloss or facet is supplied.

findings.title: Faith and the Risk of Arrest
findings.claim: The focus believer and purposeful course can be read as countering arrest: 17:22 sets divided dependence on a path toward blame, sitting, and abandonment.
findings.mechanism: The prohibition and its consequence in 17:22 give the focus trust/belief and movement an independent counter-pattern. The attributed trace reads sitting as withdrawal and abandonment as support failure.
findings.reader_payoff: Belief is not merely a doctrinal label beside self-powered work; it can frame the conditions under which a course remains mobile.
findings.containment: Sitting may be an idiom for condemned status rather than kinetic commentary. The weakening-legs image is HFT's metaphor for abandonment, not a literal gloss of the supplied word. Do not infer that belief alone is sufficient.

epistemic.reason: The 17:22 surface and trace coordinates agree, but its kinetic application to the focus is explicitly attributed.

branch_activations.carrier: The directed-worship forms at 17:22:4-5, as described in the trace.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus belief can be read against a dependence that ends in arrest.
branch_activations.boundary: No registry gloss or facet is supplied for the worship cue.

branch_activations.carrier: The sitting form at 17:22:7, traced as withdrawal from action.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus course is contrasted with sitting withdrawal.
branch_activations.boundary: The unresolved trace does not establish a separate lexical branch gloss.

findings.reader_payoff: The focus verb can carry an image of responsive amplification, not only spoken praise or later payment.

findings.title: Striving as Analogical Self-Release
findings.claim: The focus effort can be pictured as labor toward release from an attached, nontransferable account, with that release-directed work itself acknowledged.

findings.reader_payoff: The effort becomes more than generic merit accumulation: it is a course directed toward release from personal encumbrance.
findings.containment: The emancipation image is analogical only. The focus does not establish a literal manumission transaction, and the unresolved context branches remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: The technical labor branch is registered, but its application to the nearby account and burden is an attributed cross-domain analogy.

findings.title: Belief as the Counterpart to Denial
findings.claim: 17:10 pairs denial of the Hereafter with painful punishment; 17:19 names desire for that horizon, striving toward it, and a believer whose effort is acknowledged.
findings.mechanism: The non-belief form and Hereafter term in 17:10 independently meet the focus believer and later-horizon forms, making belief a positive counterpart within a three-part course of desire, effort, and belief.
findings.reader_payoff: Belief is a structural condition in the focus's response to the Hereafter, not merely a detachable doctrinal modifier.
findings.containment: This contrast does not say that belief alone suffices: the focus also names desire and striving. It makes no further claim about the exact nature of punishment or reward.

epistemic.reason: The contrast is directly present in the supplied Arabic of both native context and focus.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: dogru sayip kabul etme

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 17:10 names those who do not believe in the Hereafter and the painful consequence.
branch_activations.activation: The direct denial/affirmation contrast returns through the focus's believer and desired-horizon words.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus belief belongs to the positive response to the Hereafter alongside desire and effort.
branch_activations.boundary: No claim is made that belief by itself fulfills all the focus conditions.

findings.title: Help-Seeking Beside Striving
findings.claim: As an external overlay, Fātiḥa 1:5 places communal worship beside an explicit plea for aid; this can frame the focus's active striving as compatible with seeking help rather than self-sufficient exertion.
findings.mechanism: The focus effort form supplies purposeful movement, while 1:5's service and help-seeking forms independently add a relation of dependence around that activity.
findings.reader_payoff: The overlay makes assistance-seeking perceptible alongside acknowledged effort without displacing the native guidance context.
findings.containment: This is an analogy, not lexical equivalence, quotation, or a claim that 17:19 explicitly requires the Fātiḥa plea. Native 17:9 already supplies guidance; 1:6-7 largely restate that contact and add no separate overlay.

epistemic.reason: The external wording is direct, but its relation to the focus is a bounded cross-ayah analogy.

branch_activations.carrier: The focus effort forms purposeful movement toward its stated end.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Fātiḥa 1:5 places communal service beside a direct plea for help.
branch_activations.activation: The plea for assistance meets the focus movement as a relation of striving that need not be self-sufficient.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus effort can be viewed alongside dependence and aid-seeking.
branch_activations.boundary: The external relation is analogical only and supplies no new lexical sense for the focus verb.

friction_notes: The focus word alignment resolves 17 of 17 units. Legacy-unbound HFT context traces have exact supplied Arabic, word indices, and roots, but no independent target morphology; unresolved registry branches therefore use null glosses/facets and attributed activation.
The packet supplies commentary_obligation review labels but no semantic_obligations or required_branch_facets arrays. No obligation identifiers or unprovided facets were invented.

The only candidate branch excluded is root_000610/B003: its boundary excludes psychological willing, while the focus carrier is Form IV willing. In the external phase, 1:5 adds the aid-seeking relation; 1:6-7 repeat the native guidance contact in 17:9, and 1:2-4 add no distinct landed contact.
